reason: The cited evidence shows ML can predict phases and properties in HEAs (E2, E3) and that feature selection aids interpretability (E1), but none provides specific support for extracting hierarchical features from HfNbTiVAl10, predicting fracture behavior, or achieving >10× speedup and higher accuracy over established simulations for this specific alloy.
premises: Quantitative microstructural features (grain size, interfaces, precipitates) can be extracted from HfNbTiVAl10's hierarchical heterostructure.
An ML model trained on these features can predict Young's modulus, yield strength, and fracture behavior.
The ML model will be >10× faster than established multi-scale simulations.
The ML model will have higher accuracy than established multi-scale simulations.
Physics-informed microstructural features can capture strengthening mechanisms (solid-solution, grain-boundary, precipitation) as a proxy for detailed simulations.
